chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajli said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the redness (of sunset) disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, then the sun has set in the east of the earth.'

key_terms.اَلْحُمْرَةُ: The redness of the sky after sunset, used as a visual indicator for sunset time.

ai.seo_question: How to determine the exact time of sunset for Maghrib prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific astronomical indicator for Maghrib prayer, distinguishing the disappearance of the 'redness' (al-humra) in the east from the general sunset. In Shia fiqh, this helps resolve the difference of opinion regarding whether Maghrib begins at the disappearance of the sun's disk or the subsequent redness, emphasizing the visual confirmation of the sun's complete descent. This practical guidance ensures accurate timing for the first daily prayer, reflecting the Imams' attention to precise ritual observance.
